item.title: Nilpotent Deformation Theory via Ultrasolid Algebra
item.description: arXiv:2610.20801v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deformation theory studies how varieties and other algebro-geometric objects vary in families. A central part of the subject is formal deformation theory, where one deforms over an Artinian base; such deformation problems are governed by Lie algebraic models. We pose the question of deforming varieties over nilpotent but not necessarily Artinian bases. These turn out to be classified by the same Lie algebraic models plus some topological structure. More precisely, we will consider partition Lie algebroids in the category of ultrasolid modules, a variation of the solid modules of Clausen and Scholze that give a well-behaved category akin to topological modules. To approach this result, we decompose deformation problems into n-nilpotent layers. Each of these layers is individually easier to understand, and is classified by simpler variants of partition Lie algebras.
item.dc:creator: Sof\'ia Marlasca Aparicio

item.title: Linear Independence of Polynomial Compositions with Bounded Input Degree
item.description: arXiv:2610.20825v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the weak composition-independence conjectures of Kohn, Marchetti, Massarenti and Mella. The proof uses deformations of rational curves and a single kernel of the linearized equation. Riemann-Roch gives a contradiction from tangent fields with controlled poles. By settling these conjectures, we prove that a neural network with a general polynomial activation function of sufficiently large degree is identifiable.
item.dc:creator: Xiaotian Chang, Yacoub Hendi

item.title: Normal complex surface singularities with rational homology disk smoothings
item.description: arXiv:2610.20991v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a normal surface singularity whose minimal good resolution graph has at least two nodes does not admit a rational homology disk smoothing. Together with the earlier graph classifications and the analytic classifications of Fowler and Wahl, this gives a complete classification of normal surface singularities admitting rational homology disk smoothings and proves Wahl's conjecture. The same argument also proves Wahl's Rational Conjecture.
item.dc:creator: M\'arton Beke, Heesang Park, Dongsoo Shin, Andr\'as I. Stipsicz

item.title: A $p$-adic Riemann--Hilbert correspondence over Robba rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.21065v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct overconvergent period sheaves $\mathcal{O}\widetilde{\mathbb{C}}^{I,\dagger}$ and $\mathcal{O}\mathbb{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}^{\dagger,+}$ on the $v$-site of a liftable semi-stable formal scheme $\mathfrak{X}_Z$. By establishing a decompletion theorem for small representations, we prove a $p$-adic Riemann-Hilbert correspondence relating small $\widetilde{\mathbb{C}}^I$-local systems (resp. $\mathbb{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}^+$-local systems) on the generic fiber $X_Z$ to small flat connections on the associated period ringed spaces. We further analyze the local Frobenius action and show that this correspondence is compatible with the Frobenius structure. As an application, we prove a comparison theorem between the cohomology of these period sheaves and the rigid cohomology of the special fiber, refining results of Le Bras and Colmez--Nizio{\l}.
item.dc:creator: Zekun Chen, Ruochuan Liu, Yupeng Wang, Jiahong Yu, Xinwen Zhu

item.title: Positivity of Wahl defects and representations from index-one covers
item.description: arXiv:2610.21092v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let \((X,E) \to (V,0)\) be the minimal good resolution of a normal complex surface singularity, with \(E\) reduced. The Wahl defect is \(\Delta(V,0) :=h^1(\mathcal{O}_X)-h^1(S_X)+h^1(\bigwedge^2 S_X)\), where \(S_X=\Theta_X(-\log E)\). For non-Gorenstein \(\mathbb{Q}\)-Gorenstein singularities \((V,0)\), we prove that \(\Delta(V,0)\geq0\), with equality precisely in the quasi-homogeneous case. This proves Wahl's Main Conjecture in this class and his \(\mathbb{Q}\)-Gorenstein and Rational Conjectures. The proof expresses \(\Delta\) as the multiplicity of the canonical character in a representation constructed from differential forms and residues. We also prove \(\Delta+4p_g\geq0\) for arbitrary normal surface singularities, with equality precisely for rational quasi-homogeneous singularities. For smoothings of rational surface singularities, we give a Riemann--Roch formula for the lengths of the cokernels of the restriction maps to the central fiber for all reflexive canonical powers, in terms of the Milnor number and periodic local Riemann--Roch corrections. This yields numerical and representation-theoretic criteria for \(\mathbb{Q}\)-Gorenstein smoothings, defined as quotients of equivariant smoothings of the index-one cover with trivial group action on the base. If a rational singularity admits a \(\mathbb{Q}\)-Gorenstein smoothing, such smoothings are precisely those with minimal Milnor number, or equivalently those whose smoothing components have minimal dimension. Combining these results, we prove that every rational homology disk smoothing is \(\mathbb{Q}\)-Gorenstein, has a rational weighted homogeneous central fiber, and occurs over a one-dimensional smoothing component. Together with the known weighted homogeneous classification, this completes the analytic classification of normal surface singularities admitting rational homology disk smoothings.
item.dc:creator: Heesang Park, Dongsoo Shin

item.title: Nonlinear neighborhoods of smooth curves and arbitrarily negative Wahl defects
item.description: arXiv:2610.21093v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a theory of nonlinear neighborhoods of smooth projective curves of genus at least two, constructed by gluing products of open subsets of a curve with a disc using nonlinear changes of the disc coordinate. Their zero sections have normal bundles of negative degree and contract to normal surface singularities. For the minimal good resolution \((X,E) \to (V,0)\) of a normal complex surface singularity other than a rational double point, the Wahl defect is defined by \(\Delta(V,0) := h^1(\mathcal{O}_X)-h^1(S_X)+h^1(\bigwedge^2S_X)\), where \(E\) is reduced and \(S_X = \Theta_X(-\log E)\). We give a finite formula for this defect in terms of extension obstructions when \(E\) is a single smooth curve. For our constructed neighborhoods, the formula involves extensions of functions alone, includes obstructions at every order, and gives a sharp lower bound depending only on the genus. We apply the theory to hyperelliptic curves and smooth plane curves. Both families consist of singularities that are neither \(\mathbb{Q}\)-Gorenstein nor quasi-homogeneous. The hyperelliptic examples realize every nonpositive integer as a Wahl defect and attain the genus bound in every genus at least two. They disprove Wahl's Main Conjecture, which asserts nonnegativity for non-Gorenstein singularities, with equality precisely in the quasi-homogeneous case.
item.dc:creator: Heesang Park, Dongsoo Shin

item.title: A refinement of the strange duality conjecture on K3 surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.21272v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $v,w$ be primitive Mukai vectors of positive rank on a polarized K3 surface with $\chi(v\otimes w)=0$. Marian and Oprea conjectured that the strange duality map $H^0(M(v),\Theta_w)^\vee\to H^0(M(w),\Theta_v)$ is either zero or an isomorphism. We give three families of counterexamples to this conjecture. In each of them the map is nonzero but fails to be an isomorphism: in the first (a quartic surface) it is not surjective; in the second (Picard rank one, including very general polarized K3 surfaces) the source has strictly larger dimension than the target; and in the third (an elliptic surface) source and target both have dimension six, yet the map has rank five. The three examples share a common mechanism: one of the moduli spaces carries an effective divisor of square $-2$ on which a theta line bundle has negative degree, so that this theta line bundle is not nef and has nonvanishing higher cohomology, and the theta sections produced by the strange duality map vanish to excess order along this divisor. We therefore propose a refined conjecture, in which both theta line bundles are assumed to be big and nef, for instance ample.
item.dc:creator: Shizhuo Zhang, Yu Zhao

item.title: Fundamental Groups and Coregularity: Klt Pairs with Trivial and Nef Log-Anticanonical Class
item.description: arXiv:2610.21358v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we study how the absolute coregularity of a projective log pair reflects on its fundamental group. More precisely, we show that for a projective klt log pair $(X,D)$ of absolute coregularity $c$ and arbitrary dimension the fundamental group $\pi_1^{\rm reg}(X,D)$ admits a normal abelian subgroup of finite index and rank at most $2c$. We reduce this statement to klt Calabi-Yau pairs with standard coefficients of dimension $c$. In the cases $0\le c\le2$ and fixed dimension, we can furthermore bound the index of a solvable normal subgroup. Combining the reduction with the recent regular-locus theorem of Fu-Guo-Song-Wang, we prove the coregularity bound in every dimension. In particular, for a projective klt pair $(X,D)$ with $-(K_X+D)$ nef, the orbifold fundamental group of the smooth locus is virtually abelian of rank at most $2\, {\rm dim}X$.
item.dc:creator: Lukas Braun, Fernando Figueroa

item.title: Good stratifications of non-degenerate locally tame complete intersection varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.21446v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we show that non-degenerate locally tame complete intersection varieties admit good stratifications. As an application, we study variation of the Milnor fibrations in pencils associated with non-degenerate hypersurface singularities.
item.dc:creator: Kazumasa Inaba

item.title: Complete homogeneous varieties over a field
item.description: arXiv:2610.21497v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The main objects of this paper are complete homogeneous varieties under the action of a semisimple group $G$ over field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. When the isotropy groups of the geometric points are smooth parabolics, these are classically known as twisted flag varieties and are well studied in the literature. If the smoothness assumption is removed, we get a larger class of varieties which we call as \emph{twisted parabolic varieties}. The main goal of this paper is to study the structure, classification and properties of these varieties. We first understand their structure over a separable closure of $k$ by classifying non-smooth parabolics containing a Borel; this builds on the recently completed classification of such parabolics over an algebraically closed field. Then, via Galois descent we get a combinatorial criterion for such a variety to descend over $k$. We compute the Picard group of twisted parabolic varieties by embedding them into products of twisted flag varieties, study their local rigidity properties and show that they are rational if they have a $k$-rational point for $p \geq 3$. When $k$ is perfect, we show many interesting properties such as existence of a universal purely inseparable cover, transitivity of $k$-rational points under $G(k)$ as well as the existence of a smooth parabolic in the stabilizer of every such point. However, these properties fail if $k$ is imperfect and we demonstrate this with illuminating examples.
item.dc:creator: Michel Brion, Matilde Maccan, Srinivasan Srimathy

item.title: Quotients of Calabi-Yau Generalized Fermat manifolds and Log Enriques varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.21752v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Enriques manifolds and Log Enriques varieties have attracted a lot of interest in the last years. In this paper we study Enriques manifolds and Log Enriques varieties that are respectively \'etale and quasi-\'etale quotients of Calabi-Yau manifolds. We produce several examples by studying quotients of generalized Fermat manifolds of Calabi-Yau type. These are complete intersections of Fermat type manifolds all of the same degree and were described recently by Hidalgo, Hughes and Leyton-\'Alvarez. We describe all their quotients by a fixed-point-free automorphism. Most of the quotients are Log Enriques varieties or Calabi-Yau varieties with terminal singularities. In one case we get a family of Enriques manifolds which is a subfamily of a family described previously by Boissi\`ere, Camere and the third author, which is one of the two so far known families of Enriques manifolds of Calabi-Yau type. This family is obtained as an \'etale quotient of order two of a Calabi-Yau manifold complete intersection of quadrics, the other family is the Hilbert scheme of $n$ points on an Enriques surface. In the last part of the paper we show that these two families are different by computing their second Betti numbers, which are equal to one and eleven respectively.
item.dc:creator: Simone Billi, Ana Julisa Palomino, Alessandra Sarti

item.title: The linear positive torsor presentation and arithmetic purity of strong approximation
item.description: arXiv:2610.21762v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we define a notion for varieties called linear positive torsor presentation. For varieties with a linear positive torsor presentation over number fields, we establish the arithmetic purity of strong approximation with the Brauer--Manin obstruction off the empty set. As a consequence, we recover arithmetic purity for smooth toric variety with no non-constant global section. Moreover, we classify the chain connected class for rational points on such varieties over any field of characteristic zero.
item.dc:creator: Yijin Wang

item.title: The space of polarized compactifications of an affine variety
item.description: arXiv:2610.21838v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X$ be a normal affine variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Through the lens of non-Archimedean geometry, we study the space of polarized compactifications of $X$, consisting of pairs $(\bar X, D)$ where $\bar X$ is a normal projective variety containing $X$ as a dense open subset, and $D$ is an effective ample $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor with support equal to the complement of $X$ in $\bar X$. We identify this space with a natural class of functions--the Fubini--Study functions--on the Berkovich analytification of $X$. Through a Rees correspondence, we also give a bijection with the space of homogeneous $\mathbb{Q}$-valued, finitely generated negative non-Archimedean norms (or filtrations) on the coordinate ring of $X$. Using the above identifications, we equip the space of polarized compactifications, and numerical classes thereof, with natural metrics and identify the metric completions. The latter include a space of continuous plurisubharmonic functions in the sense of Chambert-Loir and Ducros, and a space of birational curve classes as studied by Dang and Favre.
item.dc:creator: Mattias Jonsson, Yueqiao Wu

item.title: Reconstruction of Fano manifolds from the orthogonal to an exceptional vector bundle
item.description: arXiv:2610.21904v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X$ and $Y$ be smooth complex Fano manifolds of dimension at least three with very ample anticanonical bundles and let $V_X$ and $V_Y$ be exceptional vector bundles on $X$ and $Y$, respectively. We prove that a Fourier--Mukai equivalence $V_X^\perp\simeq V_Y^\perp$ implies $X\simeq Y$.
item.dc:creator: Songtao Kenneth Ma

item.title: Deep Learning of Topological Equivalence Classes
item.description: arXiv:2610.21981v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate an application of deep learning to the problem of identifying whether two generating vectors correspond to topologically equivalent finite group actions on Riemann surfaces, showing how architectures developed for semantic understanding have use for pure mathematical problems. In doing so we discuss how desired algebraic structure influences model design, and explore which structural properties of topological equivalence classes the model has successfully learnt.
item.dc:creator: Linden Disney-Hogg, Max Zuev

item.title: Perfectoid Pure and Signature Pairs
item.description: arXiv:2610.22059v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend perfectoid purity and related invariants to divisor pairs in mixed characteristic. The resulting purity condition agrees with $F$-purity of pairs in characteristic $p$ as defined by Hara--Watanabe. For normal (respectively, demi-normal) log $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein pairs, we show that perfectoid pure implies log canonical (respectively, semi-log canonical). We similarly establish adjunction for perfectoid pure pairs and inversion of adjunction for principal pairs in complete intersections along a Cartier divisor. We also define perfectoid pure thresholds and prove localization and base change results, including a formula for local extensions with regular closed fiber. We establish upper bounds in terms of analytic spread, dimension, and log canonical thresholds. Finally, we also introduce perfectoid signatures for divisor pairs in mixed characteristic whose positivity characterizes the BCM-regularity of log $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein pairs. We prove a transformation rule under finite extensions and show continuity and convexity for scalings of a Cartier divisor.
item.dc:creator: Hanlin Cai, Anne Fayolle, Linquan Ma, Karl Schwede, Ilya Smirnov, Kevin Tucker, Joe Waldron

item.title: The monodromy conjecture for high order poles, and norms of residue antiderivatives
item.description: arXiv:2610.22111v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the strong local monodromy conjecture for poles of order at least $n-1$ of the naive motivic zeta-function for a complex polynomial of $n$ variables. Moreover, for every such pole $s$, we construct an explicit homology $\exp(2\pi i s)$-eigencycle in a neighborhood of any given 1-dimensional exceptional stratum contributing the pole. The proof combines topological techniques developed by the author with a fact of birational geometry discovered by AI.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Esterov

item.title: Gluing weak approximability along recollements
item.description: arXiv:2610.22161v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study whether weak approximability glues along recollements of triangulated categories that are compactly generated by a single object. This is applied to derived categories of complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology and prescribed support for quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic spaces.
item.dc:creator: Pat Lank

item.title: Series of Fano quiver moduli from extended Dynkin quivers
item.description: arXiv:2610.22203v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Associated to small extended Dynkin quivers, we construct series of Fano varieties of fixed Picard rank at most five and arbitrary even dimension, which admit a very explicit description of their geometry. For example, they all admit a flat morphism to a projective space, whose general fiber is a product of projective lines. We also give a closed formula for all Betti numbers, and interpret this formula in terms of an action of a cohomological Hall algebra on the cohomology of all the varieties in a series.
item.dc:creator: Pieter Belmans, Markus Reineke

item.title: Deterministic Determination of Axial Constants, Sectional Regularities and Annihilator Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.22251v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Axial constants and sectional regularities are recently introduced invariants of homogeneous polynomial ideals that, like the already earlier introduced annihilator numbers, depend on generic choices of coordinates. We provide effective characterisations of the genericity underlying these invariants in terms of $\beta$-maximal position and strong stability. In particular, we show that $\beta$-maximal position suffices for determining generic annihilator numbers and sectional regularities, while its combination with strong stability yields corresponding results for axial constants. We also develop deterministic linear algebra procedures for detecting the required generic positions and for computing these invariants.
item.dc:creator: Amir Hashemi, Rozhin Sadr, Werner M. Seiler

item.title: Tensor-generating line bundles on toric varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.22279v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A line bundle is $\otimes$-generating if its powers generate the derived category of perfect complexes. Refining the derived Nakai--Moishezon criterion of Ito--Olander, we characterize $\otimes$-generating line bundles on proper toric varieties by a combinatorial criterion on the fan, leading to the notion of $\otimes$-generating fans characterizing $\otimes$-generating canonical bundles. Furthermore, we prove an analogue of Kleiman's criterion of ampleness for $\otimes$-generation. As applications, we provide several examples including: (i) smooth proper fourfolds with no $\otimes$-generating line bundle, by showing that products of two or more positive-dimensional proper toric varieties admit a $\otimes$-generating line bundle only when they are projective, (ii) families of smooth non-projective proper threefolds with $\otimes$-generating canonical bundles. Finally, we study subvarieties obstructing $\otimes$-generation of canonical bundles and implications to autoequivalences of derived categories.
item.dc:creator: Daigo Ito, Michael R. Zeng, Xiangru Zeng

item.title: Integral and higher-genus quantum McKay correspondence in type D
item.description: arXiv:2610.22359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish Iritani's integral form of the $\mathbb{C}^\times$-equivariant Crepant Transformation Conjecture (CTC) for the minimal resolution of the surface singularity $\mathbb{C}^2/\mathbb{BD}_{4n}$, where $\mathbb{BD}_{4n}$ is the binary dihedral group of order $4n$. We then use Givental's quantisation formalism to prove the all-genus full-descendent CTC in that case. As an application, we deduce the Bryan-Cadman-Young degree-zero form of the orbifold Gromov-Witten/Donaldson-Thomas correspondence for the Calabi-Yau 3-orbifold $[\mathbb{C}^2/\mathbb{BD}_{4n}] \times \mathbb{C}$.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Brini, Jingxiang Ma

item.title: Holomorphy rings and the Nullstellensatz over large fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.21039v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For an infinite field $K$ and an ideal $I\subseteq K[X_1,\dots,X_n]$, let $J(Z_K(I))$ be the ideal of polynomials vanishing on the $K$-rational zero locus of $I$. A Nullstellensatz over $K$ is an algebraic description of this closure operator on ideals. Hilbert's classical theorem provides such a description via the radical of $I$ over any algebraically closed field. In the present article, we introduce a unifying framework for Nullstellens\"atze over arbitrary rings using the notion of an $A$-radical, for $A$ is a subring of $K(X)$ containing $K[X]$. We show that a single canonical holomorphy ring gives a Nullstellensatz over every infinite field, recovering Hilbert's theorem when $K$ is algebraically closed. In addition, we give a new characterization of large fields (in the sense of Pop) via a particular Nullstellensatz: a perfect field is large exactly when the \emph{rational} holomorphy ring $A_n(K)$--the intersection of all $K$-rational places of residue field exactly $K$--satisfies the corresponding Nullstellensatz. Finally we study the order structure of the class of rings $A$ for which the $A$-radical gives a Nullstellensatz. We show that over non-algebraically closed fields this class has no minimal element, showing there is no optimal Nullstellensatz over such fields.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Cubides Kovacsics, Sebasti\'an Uribe Rinc\'on

item.title: Coefficient lifting for skew divided differences and triple Schubert coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.21053v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Skew divided difference operators \(\partial_{w/v}\), introduced by Macdonald, play an important role in the study of Schubert polynomials and their structure constants. For permutations \(u,v,w\in S_n\), we show that the coefficient of each monomial \(\xx^\alpha\) in \(\partial_{w/v}\SSch_u(\xx;\yy)\), where \(\SSch_u(\xx;\yy)\) is the double Schubert polynomial, is a single triple Schubert coefficient evaluated at \(\tb=0\), whose indices form an explicit lift of \((u,v,w)\) to \(S_{n+\abs{\alpha}}\). As an application, we show that every coefficient of \(\partial_{w/v}\SSch_u(\xx)\) is a single Schubert structure constant. This gives a new proof of Kirillov's conjecture that these coefficients are nonnegative.
item.dc:creator: Byung-Hak Hwang

item.title: Understanding entropy using Aubin--Yau deformations
item.description: arXiv:2610.21198v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we investigate three types of entropy that frequently appear in the research of K\"ahler geometry: the classical K\"ahler entropy, the radial entropy and the non-Archimedean entropy. We give a unifying interpretation for these entropies by showing that they can all be expressed as the derivative of the Monge--Amp\`ere energy along certain Aubin--Yau type deformations. Such considerations also lead to a novel algebraic criterion for the existence of constant scalar curvature K\"ahler metrics.
item.dc:creator: Tam\'as Darvas, Kewei Zhang

item.title: Asymptotics of the Moduli Spaces of Parabolic $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb C)$-Higgs Bundles
item.description: arXiv:2610.21303v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the large-scale geometry of the moduli spaces of stable strongly parabolic $\mathrm{SL}(3,\C)$-Higgs bundles on the three-punctured sphere for a family of parabolic weights. We glue the local Toda model metric to a decoupled metric obtained from the spectral line bundle, and perturb the resulting approximate metrics to harmonic metrics adapted to the parabolic structure. We also prove that Hitchin's $L^2$ metric approaches the semi-flat metric exponentially. The metric comparison and the spectral period calculation show that each moduli space is a complete ALG gravitational instanton of type $E_6$. The asymptotic estimates are uniform on compact subintervals of the weight chamber.
item.dc:creator: Shiyu Cao

item.title: Matrix Completion Discriminants
item.description: arXiv:2610.21341v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce the matrix completion discriminant of a graph as the Zariski closure of the set of partial symmetric matrices whose completion fibers fail to meet a rank stratum transversely. A clique-sum formula for the matrix completion discriminant is established for arbitrary graphs, while explicit defining equations for cycles are obtained in terms of iterated resultants. Using these results together with the analysis of $K_4$-minor-free graphs, we prove that for every cycle-completable graph, the discriminant factors into determinant factors from maximal cliques and resultant factors from chordless cycles.
item.dc:creator: Yoshiyuki Sekiguchi, Shin-ichi Tanigawa

item.title: Frey-Mazur theorem for semistable elliptic curves over function fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.21529v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $k$ be a field, let $B/k$ be a smooth projective geometrically integral curve, and put $K=k(B)$. We prove a Frey--Mazur type theorem for nonisotrivial semistable elliptic curves over $K$. More precisely, after fixing the genus of $B$ and the characteristic of $k$, a sufficiently large prime-to-characteristic torsion representation determines the $K$-isogeny class.
item.dc:creator: Fateme Sajadi

item.title: On the variety of sum of powers of certain complete intersection forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.21544v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $F$ be a homogeneous polynomial (form). If the annihilator ideal $F^\perp$ is a complete intersection, then $F$ is called as a complete intersection form. For many complete intersection forms, we show that its minimal apolar ideal is a complete intersection and further we show that ${\rm VSP}(F)$ is irreducible and compute its dimension.
item.dc:creator: Meghana Bhat, Ronnie Sebastian

item.title: Augmentation curve for torus knots
item.description: arXiv:2610.21585v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a version of topological recursion for the correlation differentials of colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials of torus knots on the corresponding augmentation curves, following the proposal of Gu, Jockers, Klemm, and Soroush. To this end, we explicitly construct the spectral curve from the so-called auxiliary curve of Brini, Eynard, and Mari\~no and prove that it coincides with the augmentation curve for every torus knot with coprime $(r,s)$. Finally, our version of topological recursion proves the higher-genus closed-string prediction of the Aganagic--Vafa conjecture for all torus knot augmentation curves.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Hock, Sergey Shadrin

item.title: Local Tate duality for syntomic cohomology in positive characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2610.21622v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $k$ be a local field of characteristic $p>0$. We show that syntomic cohomology over $k$, with coefficients, and defined using Dodd's theory of $F$-gauges, satisfies local Tate duality. We also prove that syntomic cohomology over the ring of integers of $k$, again with coefficients, is Lagrangian with respect to the duality pairing. Finally, we show that, for $p>2$, these results recover Shatz's duality and Milne's orthogonality results for the cohomology of finite flat group schemes of $p$-power order over $k$.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Lazda

item.title: Weight structures and t-structures on the triangulated category generated by a $\mathbb{P}$-object
item.description: arXiv:2610.21859v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: $\mathbb{P}$-objects were introduced by Huybrechts and Thomas as a generalization of spherical objects. We classify the weight structures and t-structures on the triangulated category generated by a $\mathbb{P}^n[k]$-object in the sense of Krug. For $n=1$, this recovers the classification of weight structures and t-structures on the triangulated category generated by a spherical object due to Holm, Jorgensen and Yang. We also compute the Koszul-dual model of the triangulated category generated by a $\mathbb{P}^n[k]$-object.
item.dc:creator: Lukas Bonfert

item.title: A family of algebras that connects positroids, the Theta conjecture, the Delta conjecture, and Eulerian quasisymmetric functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.21894v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We define a family of algebras $\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,a,b}$ whose Hilbert series, when $n\le a+b\le n+2$, $a>0$, and $0<b<n$, enumerate certain positroid cells by codimension. Equivalently, these series enumerate certain affine permutations by length. We determine the graded $\mathfrak{S}_n$-module structure of these algebras by using exact sequences to derive an invertible recursion for their graded Frobenius characteristics when $a+b\ge n$ and then passing to the limit $a\rightarrow\infty$. In particular, the graded Frobenius characteristic $\mathrm{grFrob}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_{a+b-1}]/I_{a+b-1,a,b};q)=\operatorname{rev}_q(\omega((\Theta_{e_{a-1}}\Theta_{e_{b-1}}\nabla e_1)\mid_{t=0}))$, where $\operatorname{rev}_q$ reverses the $q$-coefficients and the specialization $(\Theta_{e_{a-1}}\Theta_{e_{b-1}}\nabla e_1)\mid_{t=0}$ appears in the Theta conjecture. For $a,b\ge1$, we also show that $e_a^\perp\mathrm{grFrob}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_{a+b}]/I_{a+b,a,b};q)=q^{\binom{a}{2}}\operatorname{rev}_q(\omega((\Delta_{e_{a-1}}^\prime e_b)\mid_{t=0}))$, where $\Delta_{e_{k-1}}^\prime e_n$ occurs in the Delta conjecture. In the three cases $a+b-n=0,1,2$, the ungraded Frobenius characteristics agree with three families of Eulerian quasisymmetric functions, respectively. We also construct an open subvariety of $(\mathbb{P}^{k-1})^n$ whose rational Chow ring is isomorphic to $\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,k,n-k}$. This variety admits a stratification induced by certain positroids. Its strata need not be affine, and their codimension generating function equals $\mathrm{Hilb}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,k,n-k};q)$.
item.dc:creator: Hai Zhu

item.title: An introduction to algebraic groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.21926v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We review the theory of abelian varieties and, more generally, algebraic groups, with a view toward arithmetic applications. We discuss their models over the rings of integers of number fields, their reductions modulo primes, their torsion points (together with their natural Galois action), and the interplay of these notions through characteristic polynomials of Frobenius.
item.dc:creator: Davide Lombardo

item.title: On the exact quantization of BCOV Theory on Calabi-Yau Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.21927v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We announce the solution of constructing perturbative quantum BCOV invariants on arbitrary Calabi-Yau manifolds. In this note, we outline the construction and present an explicit solution. The quantization includes all descendant fields and all loop orders, and expresses the quantum BCOV interaction by an explicit integration over the moduli space of marked Riemann surfaces. This canonical solution provides a mathematical construction of all higher genus BCOV invariants on compact Calabi-Yau manifolds, which are conjecturally equivalent to all higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants on the mirror.
item.dc:creator: Si Li, Minghao Wang

item.title: The derived category of a generalized complex torus
item.description: arXiv:2610.21960v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For any translation invariant generalized complex structure J on a torus we construct the derived category D(J) generalizing the derived category of coherent sheaves on a complex torus and the affine/convergent Fukaya category of a symplectic torus. The category is defined in terms of a non-commutative curved deformation of the Dolbeault algebra of a complex torus. We show that this category is independent of the chosen deformation path, which we prove using non-commutative Fourier-Mukai duality. We also prove that the action of O(2n,2n; Z) on the space of generalized complex structures leaves the category D(J) invariant. In particular, T-duality acts trivially on D(J). We construct concrete objects associated to affine Lagrangians in the derived category associated to a symplectic torus and show that their spaces of morphisms are given by Floer cohomology. We show that our construction is consistent with the homological mirror symmetry conjecture (including its non-commutative version).
item.dc:creator: Patrick Antweiler, Vicente Cort\'es, Julian Holstein, Markus R\"oser, Aldo Witte

item.title: Variation of Shafarevich-Tate groups in Hida families
item.description: arXiv:2610.22226v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathbf{f}$ be a Hida family of cusp forms over a standard (power series) Iwasawa algebra. We determine the pseudo-isomorphism class of the big Shafarevich-Tate group attached to $\mathbf{f}$ over a suitable imaginary quadratic field by describing all its higher Fitting ideals; this description is given in terms of the universal Kolyvagin system of Howard's big Heegner points. As a second contribution, we study the variation of the structure of the Shafarevich-Tate groups of the classical specializations of $\mathbf{f}$.
item.dc:creator: Enrico Da Ronche, Matteo Longo, Stefano Vigni, Francesco Zerman

item.title: Stratification of opers with apparent singularities and isomonodromic bubbling
item.description: arXiv:2610.22326v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: On a compact Riemann surface of genus $g \geq 2$, we study Simpson's stratification of the de Rham moduli space of rank-2 flat connections. Upon representing flat $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$-connections by branched projective structures, or equivalently by opers with apparent singularities, the stratum containing a flat connection is determined by the minimal number of apparent singularities needed to represent it. We construct explicit holomorphic families in which two simple apparent singularities collide and disappear, so that the family crosses into a smaller stratum; this realizes Simpson's closure relation between strata near generic points. The analogous families of Higgs bundles are described by Baker--Akhiezer divisors on the spectral curve in which two points converge to a pair of points exchanged by the spectral involution. We show that, before the collision, the two apparent singularities are joined by twin paths bounding a bubble, so that these families arise from the isomonodromic bubbling surgery discussed by Calsamiglia, Deroin and Francaviglia.
item.dc:creator: Duong Dinh, Troy Figiel, Joerg Teschner

item.title: On the fundamental groups of subelliptic varieties
item.description: arXiv:2212.07085v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the fundamental group of any smooth subelliptic variety is finite. Moreover, it is also proved that every finite group can be realized as the fundamental group of a smooth subelliptic variety. As a consequence, it follows that there exists a smooth subelliptic variety homotopy equivalent to the $n$-sphere if and only if $n>1$. This result can be considered as a negative answer to the algebraic version of Gromov's problem on the homotopy types of Oka manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Yuta Kusakabe

item.title: On higher Pythagoras numbers of real polynomial rings
item.description: arXiv:2311.07356v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the higher Pythagoras numbers for the polynomial ring are infinite $p_{2s}(K[x_1,x_2,\dots,x_n])=\infty$ provided that $K$ is a formally real field, $n\geq2$ and $s\geq 1$. This almost fully solves an old question \cite[Problem 8]{cldr1982}. The remaining open cases are precisely $n=1$ and $s>1$. Moreover, we study in detail the cone of binary octics that are sums of fourth powers of quadratic forms. We determine its facial structure as well as its algebraic boundary. This can also be seen as sums of fourth powers of linear forms on the second Veronese of $\mathbb{P}^1$. As a result, we disprove a conjecture of Reznick \cite[Conjecture 7.1]{reznick2011} which states that if a binary form $f$ is a sum of fourth powers, then it can be written as $f=f_1^2+f_2^2$ for some nonnegative forms $f_1,f_2$.
item.dc:creator: Tomasz Kowalczyk, Julian Vill

item.title: Fppf-descent for condensed animated rings
item.description: arXiv:2311.13408v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we define "animated affinoid algebras" and prove some basic properties of them. Then we generalize the result of the previous paper of the author and the result of Lucas Mann (fppf-descent for discrete rings or affinoid algebras) to discrete animated rings or animated affinoid algebras.
item.dc:creator: Yutaro Mikami

item.title: Minimal energy local systems on curves
item.description: arXiv:2503.19250v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\Sigma_{g,n}$ be an orientable topological surface of genus $g$ with $n$ punctures. When $g = 0$, Deroin and Tholozan studied the class of supra-maximal representations $\pi_1(\Sigma_{0,n})\to \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$, and they showed that the supra-maximal representations form a compact component of a real relative character variety. We study a collection of rank $r$ local systems on $\Sigma_{g,n}$ which we call of minimal energy. These are generalizations of supra-maximal representations, and underlie polarizable complex variations of Hodge structure for any choice of complex structure on $\Sigma_{g,n}$. Like the supra-maximal representations, the minimal energy local systems form compact components of relative character varieties of real forms of $\mathrm{GL}_r(\mathbb{C})$. We show that when the local monodromy data around the punctures is chosen to be unitary and generic, and the relative character variety is nonempty, these minimal energy local systems always exist. When $g > 0$, we show that the minimal energy local systems come from unitary representations of $\pi_1(\Sigma_{g,n})$. If $g = 0$ we show that they do not always come from unitary representations, and we study their structure in general.
item.dc:creator: Charlie Wu

item.title: Hypergeometric local systems and parabolic bundles
item.description: arXiv:2509.25629v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Beukers and Heckman gave necessary and sufficient conditions for a hypergeometric function $_n F_{n-1}$ to be algebraic. We give a new proof of this theorem by passing through the Mehta-Seshadri correspondence. In particular, we explicitly write down the parabolic bundle corresponding to a unitary hypergeometric local system.
item.dc:creator: Charlie Wu

item.title: Kernels of Arithmetic Jet Spaces and Frobenius Morphism
item.description: arXiv:2601.22591v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For any $\pi$-formal group scheme $G$, the Frobenius morphism between arithmetic jet spaces restricts to generalized kernels of the projection map. Using the functorial properties of such kernels of arithmetic jet spaces, we show that this morphism is indeed induced by a natural ring map between shifted $\pi$-typical Witt vectors. In the special case when $G = \hat{\mathbb{G}}_a$, the arithmetic jet space, as well as the generalized kernels are affine $\pi$-formal planes with Witt vector addition as the group law. In that case the above morphism is the multiplication by $\pi$ map on Witt vector schemes. In fact, the system of arithmetic jet spaces and generalized kernels of any $\pi$-formal group scheme $G$ along with their maps and identitites satisfied among them are a generalization of the case of the Witt vector scheme with the system of maps such as the Frobenius, Verschiebung and multiplication by $\pi$.
item.dc:creator: Rajat Kumar Mishra, Arnab Saha

item.title: Two-step nilpotent monodromy of local systems on special varieties
item.description: arXiv:2603.14539v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We address a question of Campana by giving a criterion for when nilpotent local systems on quasi-projective varieties have 2-step nilpotent monodromy. As an application, we prove that the monodromy group of any complex local system on smooth complex quasi-projective variety that is special in the sense of Campana or $h$-special (e.g. containg a Zariski dense entire curve), is virtually 2-step nilpotent. This result sharply refines a theorem of Cadorel, Yamanoi, and the second author. To establish this result, we develop a deformation theory for certain local systems on quasi-compact K\"ahler manifolds by constructing universal deformations for such local systems.
item.dc:creator: Junyan Cao, Ya Deng, Christopher D. Hacon, Mihai Paun

item.title: A note on complex Lie Algebras isomorphic to their conjugate
item.description: arXiv:2604.06979v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A real Lie algebra defines by extension of scalars a complex Lie algebra that is isomorphic to its Galois conjugate. In this paper, we are interested in the converse property: given a complex Lie algebra that is isomorphic to its conjugate, is it defined over the real numbers? We prove the existence of a $10$-dimensional nilpotent complex Lie algebra for which the answer is negative, disproving a recent conjecture by Der\'e. In addition, we compute the generic obstruction to this descent problem in terms of Brauer groups.
item.dc:creator: Cyril Demarche

item.title: Adjoint test modules along Cohen--Macaulay morphisms
item.description: arXiv:2605.07956v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide a transformation rule for adjoint test modules along Cohen--Macaulay maps between Cohen--Macaulay varieties that have $F$-rational geometric fibers. This is, in part, an effective version of Enescu's theorem on the ascent of $F$-rationality under local maps with $F$-rational geometric fibers.
item.dc:creator: Javier Carvajal-Rojas, Axel St\"abler

item.title: Limits of Hyperk\"ahler Manifolds and Moduli Spaces of Sheaves on K3 Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2605.18065v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that a compact strongly Gauduchon manifold which is a limit of compact hyperk\"ahler manifolds is bimeromorphic to a compact hyperk\"ahler manifold. This settles a case of a conjecture of Soldatenkov and Verbitsky. A closed completion of a Gauduchon metric bounds the Dirichlet energies of nearby biholomorphisms. This bound yields a meromorphic limit map, which has degree one and is therefore a bimeromorphism onto a compact hyperk\"ahler manifold. We apply this result to moduli spaces of stable torsion-free coherent sheaves on K3 surfaces. A Bott--Chern diagonal formula gives the $\partial\bar\partial$-lemma, and positivity of determinant classes gives K\"ahlerness, proving Perego's conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Kefeng Liu, Yang Shen

item.title: On the identifiability and semi-algebraicity of ReLU neuromanifolds
item.description: arXiv:2606.02826v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study several aspects of the semi-algebraicity of the neuromanifold $\mathcal{M}_{\mathbf{d}}$ of a feedforward ReLU neural network. We prove that $\mathcal{M}_{\mathbf{d}}$ in general is not a semi-algebraic quotient of the space of parameters of the network, but it can be approximated (in a precise sense) by semi-algebraic spaces. We then consider the notion of identifiable subsets of the space of parameters, where the network does not have any hidden symmetries. We prove that the maximal identifiable subset is semi-algebraic for any neural network with semi-algebraic activation functions. Lastly, we compute explicitly the identifiable subset of a shallow ReLU network and prove that for input dimensions $\ge 3$ and width $\ge 6$ it is not euclidean open.
item.dc:creator: Axel Flinth, Stefano Mereta, Michele Pernice

item.title: Local stability of Frobenius and Artin--Schreier base-change: a comparison
item.description: arXiv:2608.24256v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $(X,\Delta)\to C$ be a family of pairs over a smooth curve in positive characteristic $p>0$. We study the discrepancies of divisors over the base-change $(X,\Delta)\to C$ along Artin--Schreier and Frobenius covers of $C$, through ramification data for Artin--Schreier and degree $p$ purely inseparable extensions of DVRs. As an application, we recover a result of Hu and Zong about permanence of local stability for such base-change.
item.dc:creator: Quentin Posva

item.title: Algebraic loops, braids, and tropicalization
item.description: arXiv:2609.12074v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $Y$ be a smooth complex algebraic variety. We develop a tropical framework for studying algebraic loops, i.e., free homotopy classes in $Y^{\mathrm{an}}$ associated with formal loops $\mathrm{Spec}\, \mathbb{C}(\!(t)\!)\to Y$. When $Y$ is very affine, every formal loop determines an integral point of $\mathrm{Trop}(Y)$. For sch\"on varieties, we prove that the associated algebraic loop is determined by this tropical point together with a connected component of the corresponding initial variety. Consequently, when all initial varieties are connected, integral tropical points classify algebraic loops. We apply this theory to the case when $Y$ is a hyperplane arrangement complement. In this case, we identify the initial varieties with complements of graded arrangements and obtain explicit representatives for algebraic loops as products of relative full twists. In type $A$, these representatives recover pure algebraic braids. For root arrangements, our construction gives a tropical interpretation of the split root valuation data of Goresky, Kottwitz, and MacPherson. Finally, we prove that the cohomology of braid varieties associated with positive algebraic braids depends only on their root valuation data.
item.dc:creator: Konstantin Jakob, Masoud Kamgarpour, Ian Le, Minh-T\^am Quang Trinh

item.title: Holomorphic isomonodromic deformations of Higgs bundles: absolute lifting, spectral flatness, and nilpotent rigidity
item.description: arXiv:2609.12416v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $f:X\to S$ be a smooth projective family, and fix a semisimple flat bundle on a fiber $X_0$. Its isomonodromic deformation determines a holomorphic section $\sigma_{\mathrm{dR}}:S\to M_{\mathrm{dR}}(X/S)$ of the relative de Rham moduli space. Applying the relative non-abelian Hodge correspondence fiberwise gives a section $\sigma_{\mathrm{Dol}}:S\to M_{\mathrm{Dol}}(X/S)$, whose value at each $s\in S$ is the Higgs bundle corresponding to the flat bundle $\sigma_{\mathrm{dR}}(s)$. Unlike $\sigma_{\mathrm{dR}}$, the section $\sigma_{\mathrm{Dol}}$ is in general only real analytic. We study the geometric consequences of its holomorphicity along a complex analytic subvariety. First, we prove an absolute lifting theorem: the relative isomonodromic Higgs bundle admits an absolute Higgs lift, and the fiberwise harmonic metrics can be modified to solve the Hitchin--Simpson equation on the total space. Second, we prove that the spectral one-form on every resolved irreducible component of the relative spectral scheme is Gauss--Manin flat. As an application, we prove the nilpotent rigidity conjecture of Hu--Sun--Yang--Zuo: if the initial Higgs field is nilpotent, then the Higgs field remains nilpotent along the entire holomorphic isomonodromic locus.
item.dc:creator: Tianzhi Hu, Mai Shi, Kang Zuo

item.title: On constructibility of klt type varieties and simple $D$-module
item.description: arXiv:2610.08334v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we prove that the combination of dense klt type and $\mathcal{D}$-simplicity property establishes the klt type property.
item.dc:creator: Donghyeon Kim

item.title: Counterexamples to the Ambro--Kawamata effective non-vanishing conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.09270v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$ or $p\neq3$. We construct a terminal projective 4-fold $X$ and an ample Cartier divisor $D$ such that \[ 3K_X\sim0,\qquad D-K_X\ \text{is ample},\qquad H^0(X,D)=0. \] In char 0, this disproves Ambro--Kawamata effective non-vanishing conjecture. From this example we construct a smooth projective 4-fold $Y$ with a semiample and big Cartier divisor $D_Y$ such that $D_Y-K_Y$ is basepoint-free and big, and $H^0(Y,D_Y)=0$. We also construct a Gorenstein terminal 6-fold with $K\sim0$, other geometric avatars, and a terminal order-5 Jacobian quotient.
item.dc:creator: Rahul Ajit

item.title: Equal-mass sunset integrals and genus-zero local Gromov--Witten theory of Calabi--Yau $n$-folds
item.description: arXiv:2610.10828v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove an exact identity, as convergent logarithmic germs at large Euclidean momentum, between the equal-mass two-dimensional $(n-1)$-loop sunset Feynman integral, with $n\geq4$, and the genus-zero one-point descendant invariants of the local Calabi--Yau $n$-fold $X_n=\operatorname{Tot}(K_{F_n})$, where $F_n\subset(\mathbb P^1)^{n}$ is a smooth $(1,\ldots,1)$ hypersurface. Writing $s$ for the momentum variable and $y=-1/s$, the identity reads \[ I^{(n-1)}_{\circleddash}(s)=(-1)^{n-1}yA\,\Bigl[nR^{n-1}-\theta_Q{\mathcal D}_0^\Delta\,R^{n-2} +\sum_{j=0}^{n-3}c_jR^j\Bigr], \] where $R=\log y+O(y)$ is the local mirror coordinate, $A=\theta_yR$, $Q=e^R$, ${\mathcal D}_0^\Delta(Q)$ is the primary one-point potential, and each $c_j$ has the form \[ c_j=c_j^{(0)}+\sum_{a=0}^{n-2}\bigl(c_{j,a}\,{\mathcal D}_a^\Delta(Q) +c'_{j,a}\,\theta_Q{\mathcal D}_a^\Delta(Q)\bigr) \] with the coefficients in $\mathbb Q[\zeta(3),\zeta(5),\ldots]$ the odd zeta values coming from the Gamma class. The descendant series ${\mathcal D}_a^\Delta(Q)$ are given explicitly by the ambient hypergeometric series and the inverse mirror map. We also prove global univalence of the principal mirror map, with explicit upper and lower bounds on the $Q$-Taylor radii, extract the full primary evaluation divisor and its integral cover transform, and reduce the ambient endpoint constants to a finite universal Gamma-class part and $\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor$ real parameters.
item.dc:creator: Hartmut Maennel, Pierre Vanhove

item.title: Remarks on Lattice Actions Corresponding to Automorphism Groups of Smooth Cubic Fourfolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.19161v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The automorphism groups of smooth cubic fourfolds over the complex numbers, together with actions on defining equations, are classified in previous works. In this paper, we complete the calculation of group actions on the primitive integral cohomology lattice for all of the $156$ families in the classification. We distinguish similar families, determine the remaining action-maximal cases, and use restriction to complete the list. We also determine the generic algebraic lattices for each family. The calculation depends mainly on OSCAR.
item.dc:creator: Jie Fu

item.title: A GLSM realization of derived equivalence in $U(1) \times U(2)$ models
item.description: arXiv:2312.05740v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper studies the derived equivalence between Calabi--Yau mixed branches using the B-brane hemisphere partition function in anomalous gauged linear sigma models (GLSMs). For a family of anomalous $U(2)$ GLSMs, we study the infrared behavior of B-branes under RG flow and the variation of FI parameters in the quantum K\"ahler moduli space. As characterized by the big and small window categories of the GLSM, the RG flow effect is analyzed according to the properties of their B-brane central charges as hemisphere partition functions. The result generalizes the band restriction rules in anomalous abelian GLSMs (Clingempeel--Floch--Romo) to some $U(2)$ models. As an application, we study a family of $U(1)\times U(k)$ models for $k=1,2$, which realize a Fano UV sigma model and two IR phases as mixed branches accompanied by local Calabi--Yau Higgs components. By applying the restriction rules, we establish new derived equivalences between Calabi--Yau varieties from these anomalous models.
item.dc:creator: Jirui Guo, Ban Lin, Hao Zou

item.title: Rational points on $X_0(N)^*$ when $N$ is non-squarefree
item.description: arXiv:2505.00680v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $N$ be a positive integer and $X_0(N)^*$ be the quotient of the modular curve $X_0(N)$ by its full group of Atkin-Lehner involutions. Elkies conjectures that the rational points on $X_0(N)^*$ are only cusps or CM points when $N$ is large enough. We establish an integrality result for the $j$-invariants of non-cuspidal rational points on $X_0(N)^*$ when $N$ is non-squarefree, representing a significant step toward resolving a key subcase of Elkies' conjecture. To this end, we prove the existence of rank-zero quotients of certain modular Jacobians $J_0(pq)$. Furthermore, in the non-squarefree case we provide a complete classification of the rational points on $X_0(N)^*$ of genus $1 \leq g \leq 5$, when they are finite. In the process we identify exceptional rational points on $X_0(75)^*$ and $X_0(147)^*$ which were not known before.
item.dc:creator: Sachi Hashimoto, Timo Keller, Samuel Le Fourn

item.title: Counting rational points on non-uniruled surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2511.07060v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $X\subseteq \mathbb{P}^n$ be a non-degenerate non-uniruled irreducible projective surface of degree $d$ defined over a number field $K$, and let $N_{X^{\prime}}(B)$ be the number of rational points of $X$ of height at most $B$ that do not lie on lines contained in $X$. Assuming a suitable hypothesis on the size of the rank of Abelian varieties, we show that $N_{X^{\prime}}(B)\ll_{K,n,d,\varepsilon}B^{\frac{n+1}{n}+\varepsilon}$ for any fixed $\varepsilon>0$. In particular, if $X\subseteq \mathbb{P}^3$ is a smooth projective surface of degree $d\ge 4$ defined over a number field $K$, then $N_{X^{\prime}}(B)\ll_{K,d,\varepsilon} B^{4/3+\varepsilon}$. This conditionally improves a bound of Salberger for $d=4$ and $d=5$. The proof, based on an argument of Heath-Brown, consists of cutting $X$ by projective hyperplanes and using a uniform version of Faltings's Theorem, due to Dimitrov, Gao, and Habegger, to bound the number of rational points on the hyperplane sections of $X$.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Andreaus

item.title: Hyperplane arrangements with non-formal Milnor fibers
item.description: arXiv:2603.07301v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Each complex hyperplane arrangement $\mathcal{A}$ gives rise to a Milnor fibration of its complement. Building on work of Zuber, we give a combinatorial sufficient condition for the Milnor fiber $F(\mathcal{A})$ to be non-$1$-formal, expressed in terms of the multinet structure on $\mathcal{A}$, and use it to produce an infinite family of monomial arrangements $\mathcal{A}(3k,3k,3)$ with non-formal Milnor fibers. We also review the relevant background on cohomology jump loci, formality, and the topology of Milnor fibers of arrangements.
item.dc:creator: Alexander I. Suciu

item.title: Homological Detection by Perfectoid Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2607.17801v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We first establish estimates for the projective and injective dimensions for quotients of perfectoid algebras by radical ideals. As applications, we obtain homological characterizations of modules of finite injective dimension, (big) Cohen--Macaulay modules, Gorenstein local rings, and regular local rings in mixed characteristic in terms of perfectoid algebras. These are mixed characteristic analogues of the corresponding characterizations via Frobenius morphisms in positive characteristic.
item.dc:creator: Mohsen Asgharzadeh, Ryo Ishizuka

item.title: The Richelot isogeny graph and paramodular forms of weight 3: Atkin-Lehner signs and certified spectra
item.description: arXiv:2608.14145v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Richelot $(2,2)$-isogeny graph $G_p$ of superspecial abelian surfaces in characteristic $p$ is the genus-2 analogue of the supersingular isogeny graph: its weighted adjacency matrix is a Brandt matrix for a compact inner form of $\mathrm{GSp}_4$, and it commutes with an Atkin-Lehner involution $R(\pi)$. Refining Ibukiyama's conjectures, we conjecture the automorphic origin and the $R(\pi)$-sign of every eigenvalue: Eisenstein, Saito-Kurokawa, Yoshida and paramodular eigenvalues, and pairs of type-Va eigensystems that only $R(\pi)$ separates. We compute $G_p$ at 33 primes, with up to 2176 vertices, and certify the predicted eigenvalues and signs in exact arithmetic; at $p=167$ and $173$, where the sign prediction first becomes non-trivial, the graph carries the predicted eigenvalue $-8$ with sign $-1$. For every prime we prove that each type-Va parameter contributes exactly one eigenline of each $R(\pi)$-sign, a closed formula for the trace of $R(\pi)$, and a Fricke sign bias. If no further CAP representations occur, the non-trivial spectrum lies in $[-8\sqrt{2}, 6+4\sqrt{2}]$, both ends being sharp under the conjecture, and only Saito-Kurokawa eigenvalues exceed $8\sqrt{2}$; at all 104 primes $p\le 601$ the extreme eigenvalue computed by Florit and Smith agrees with the largest Saito-Kurokawa one. Finally, the irrational roots of the residual square factor form one Galois orbit with full symmetric Galois group at each certified prime $p\ge 29$, and the spectrum appears to follow a Plancherel law.
item.dc:creator: Hung T. Dang

item.title: Inherent Trade-offs when Enforcing Correct Data Symmetries in Multi-head Self-attention
item.description: arXiv:2608.30417v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a complete characterization of equivariant multi-head self-attention (MHSA): if an MHSA layer is equivariant to a symmetry group $G$, then $G$ can only act by permuting head-clusters, with QK and OV matrices satisfying an equivariance constraint tied to the group action. As a consequence, we prove that any fixed MHSA architecture that achieves exact equivariance by polynomially parameterizing unconstrained MHSA parameters inevitably leads to expressivity loss within the class of equivariant maps: the equivariance locus of unconstrained MHSA forms a union of extremely many Zariski-irreducible components in a reduced parameter space, and any single architecture covers at most one. For $G=D_4$ acting on $C$ copies of the regular representation as the token feature space, we show that there are $\Omega(C^{64})$ components for eight attention heads. We illustrate this with experiments on artificial tasks and show that the predicted head-cluster structures can arise naturally when the attention layer is pressured to become equivariant.
item.dc:creator: T\=ikun \^Ong, Georg B\"okman

item.title: The three- and four-loop equal-mass sunset integrals and local Calabi--Yau fourfolds and fivefolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.10821v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We determine the equal-mass two-dimensional three- and four-loop sunset Feynman integrals $I^{(3)}_\circleddash$ and $I^{(4)}_\circleddash$ at large Euclidean momentum in terms of the genus-zero Gromov--Witten theory of the local Calabi--Yau fourfold and fivefold $X_L=\operatorname{Tot}(K_{F_L})$, where $F_L\subset(\mathbb P^1)^{L+1}$, $L=3,4$, is a smooth hypersurface of multidegree $(1,\ldots,1)$. At two loops the sunset integral is governed by the prepotential of a local Calabi--Yau threefold. For $L\geq3$ the moduli spaces of unmarked stable maps have positive virtual dimension and there is no prepotential, therefore the Feynman integral is governed instead by the one-point potential $\mathcal F_{\gamma_L}$ with insertion $\gamma_L=H^{L-1}/(L-1)!$, by its gravitational descendants, and by $\zeta(3)$ boundary terms coming from the Gamma class. At both loop orders the coefficient of $R^{L-1}$ in the Frobenius expansion in the mirror coordinate $R$ is $-\theta_Q\mathcal F_{\gamma_L}$ with the Novikov variable $Q=\exp(R)$. At three loops the whole Feynman integral is an explicit expression in $\mathcal F_{\gamma_3}$ alone, because genus-zero recursion determines all descendant series from it; at four loops two diagonal series suffice, and the $\zeta(3)$ term is itself corrected by $\theta_Q\mathcal F_{\gamma_4}$. At three loops we also derive the analytic normalization independently, from the Picard--Fuchs equation and the polar part of a Mellin transform, prove integrality of the multiple-cover transforms for arbitrary integral insertions together with an explicit quantum-$K$ formula, and compute the exact period connection polynomials. Finally we give endpoint values along the Euclidean axis, bounds on the Taylor radii in the Novikov variable $Q$, a computer-assisted proof of the four-loop endpoint nonanalyticity, and a comparison of the normalizations at two, three and four loops.
item.dc:creator: Hartmut Maennel, Pierre Vanhove
